title: A linear rational coordinate with transcendental residue
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] and let $F$ be the fraction field of the polynomial ring $K[t]$ in one indeterminate [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-pc-field-extension], with $t$ explicitly the image of the polynomial indeterminate under the chosen fraction-field map. Let $O\subseteq F$ be a valuation subring, let $R=O\cap K$, and assume $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(R)}\kappa(O)=1$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then there exist $a\in K$ and $\pi\in K^\times$ such that $z=(t-a)/\pi\in O^\times$ and the residue $\bar z\in\kappa(O)$ is transcendental over $\kappa(R)$ (no nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(R)$ vanishes on it). If $t\in O$ and the prime $\mathfrak m_O\cap R[t]$ is maximal and contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$, these choices can be made with $a\in R$ and $0\ne\pi\in\mathfrak m_R$. Here a valuation subring $B$ of a field $F$ [def-weil-field] means a subring with fraction field $F$ such that, for every $z\in F^\times$, $z\in B$ or $z^{-1}\in B$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_B=B\setminus B^\times$ and its residue field is $\kappa(B)=B/\mathfrak m_B$ [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, second stage on p. 28: factorization, separable perturbation, and existence of a normalized linear function with transcendental residue, including integrality at a closed centre. Primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this exact result.

proof.text: Write $\bar{\ }$ for reduction modulo the maximal ideal. By [lem-trf-separably-closed-value-group-divisible], the value group of the separably closed valued field $(K,R)$ is divisible. The normalization conclusion of [lem-trf-residual-curve-value-group] therefore applies to every nonzero factor of a numerator or denominator: after multiplying by a constant in $K^\times$, it becomes a unit of $O$. Factoring numerator and denominator in the PID $K[t]$, every residue in $\kappa(O)$ is generated over $\kappa(R)$ by residues of normalized elements $f(t)/\pi$ with $f$ monic irreducible and $\pi\in K^\times$ chosen so that $f(t)/\pi\in O^\times$; this factor-and-residue-generation assertion is [lem-trf-normalized-polynomial-residue-generation]. Since $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(R)}\kappa(O)=1$, one of these normalized residues is transcendental over $\kappa(R)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, p. 28, paragraph beginning “Note that $\widetilde L$ is generated over $\widetilde K$” (normalization of polynomial factors).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-separable-perturbation-factor-selection] to the normalized irreducible polynomial from Step 1. Its conclusion gives a monic separable irreducible $g\in K[T]$ and $\pi\in K^\times$ such that $g(t)/\pi\in O^\times$ has transcendental residue. The same cited statement says that $g$ has degree one because $K$ is separably closed. Write $g(T)=T-a$, with $a\in K$. Then $z=(t-a)/\pi$ gives the unrestricted conclusion. The perturbation argument is confined to the cited support lemma; this step uses only its stated conclusion.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, p. 28, paragraph beginning “Moreover, we can take only separable irreducible polynomials” through “we can find $a\in K$”.

proof.text: For the closed-centre clause assume $t\in O$ and put $k=\kappa(R)$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m_O\cap R[t]$. First record the restriction identifications: for $c\in K^\times$, $c\in R^\times$ if and only if $c,c^{-1}\in O$, if and only if $c\in O^\times$. Thus $\mathfrak m_R=K\cap\mathfrak m_O$, and the quotient map embeds $k$ in $\kappa(O)$. We will use [lem-trf-valuation-inverse-maximal-ideal] for the nonunit inverse test; in particular $b\notin O$ implies $b^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_O$. These identifications need no assertion about algebraic closedness of $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, p. 28, closed-centre paragraph after the normalized linear coordinate; elementary residue computations expanded here.

proof.text: The reduction map $R[t]\to\kappa(O)$ has kernel exactly $\mathfrak p$. Since $\mathfrak p$ is maximal, $E=R[t]/\mathfrak p$ is a field embedded in $\kappa(O)$. Since $\mathfrak p\cap R=\mathfrak m_R$, the map from $R$ factors through an embedding $k\to E$, and $E$ is generated as a $k$-algebra by the image $\tau$ of $t$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zariski-lemma] to this one-generator algebra: $E/k$ is finite dimensional. In particular the powers $1,\tau,\ldots,\tau^{[E:k]}$ are linearly dependent, so the image of $t$ in $\kappa(O)$ satisfies a nonzero polynomial over $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, p. 28, closed-centre paragraph after the normalized linear coordinate; elementary residue computations expanded here.

proof.text: Keep $a,\pi,z$ from Step 2. Suppose $a\notin R$. Then $a\notin O$, so [lem-trf-valuation-inverse-maximal-ideal] gives $a^{-1}\in\mathfrak m_O$. As $t\in O$, $t/a\in\mathfrak m_O$; hence $h=1-t/a=(t-a)/(-a)$ has residue $1$ and is a unit. Indeed, if $h$ were a nonunit, both $h$ and $t/a$ would lie in the ideal $\mathfrak m_O$, forcing $1$ into that ideal. Now $z/h=-a/\pi$ is in $K\cap O^\times=R^\times$ by Step 3. Reducing $z=(-a/\pi)h$ gives $\bar z=\overline{-a/\pi}\in k$, contradicting its transcendence. Thus $a\in R$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.1, proof, p. 28, closed-centre paragraph after the normalized linear coordinate; elementary residue computations expanded here.

proof.text: Put $y=t-a\in O\setminus\{0\}$. If $y$ is a unit, then $\pi=y/z\in K\cap O^\times=R^\times$ by Step 3. Therefore $\bar z=(\tau-\bar a)/\bar\pi$ belongs to the embedded field $E$ of Step 4. Its powers are linearly dependent over $k$, since $E/k$ is finite dimensional; this contradicts transcendence. Thus $y\in\mathfrak m_O$. Apply the final clause of [lem-trf-residual-curve-value-group] to $y$: choose $0\ne c\in\mathfrak m_R$ with $z_c=y/c\in O^\times$. Then $z_c/z=\pi/c\in K\cap O^\times=R^\times$, so $\bar z_c=\overline{\pi/c}\bar z$ remains transcendental (substitution $T\mapsto\overline{\pi/c}T$ is invertible in $k[T]$). The pair $(a,c)$ is the required integral choice.
